name: Wildhammer clan
summary: In the Hinterlands, the Wildhammer clan holds to its freedom among the wooded peaks. Driven from Grim Batol centuries ago, the dwarves made Aerie Peak their home and learned to ride wild gryphons. They remain friends of the Alliance and stand ready to defend its skies.

sections.title: Exile from Grim Batol
sections.body:
Before the War of the Three Hammers, the Wildhammers lived near Ironforge. When High King Modimus Anvilmar died, civil war followed, and the victorious Bronzebeards claimed the city. Thane Khardros led his clan north and built a hold within Grim Batol. Soon, the defeated Dark Irons laid siege to it.

Khardros slew the sorceress Modgud, but her dying curse blighted the mountain and left its halls uninhabitable. The Wildhammers refused an invitation to return under Bronzebeard rule. They chose their freedom and traveled north to the forests and rocky crags of the Hinterlands.

sections.title: Riders of the Storm
sections.body:
The Wildhammers built Aerie Peak in the highlands of their new home. Unlike their kin beneath the earth, they embraced open skies and living rock, and formed a deep spiritual bond with the native gryphons. In secluded aviaries, they forged enchanted stormhammers and became Azeroth's finest aerial cavalry.

During the Second War, Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer marched toward Quel'Thalas and attacked Aerie Peak. Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar and the Alliance came to the clan's aid. In gratitude, High Thane Kurdran Wildhammer pledged his gryphon riders to the coalition. They fought the Horde's enslaved red dragons above Lordaeron and the Great Sea.

sections.title: Loyal to the End
sections.body:
When the Dark Portal reopened, Kurdran Wildhammer led his riders into Draenor with the Alliance Expedition. He gave up his return to seal the rift, and a colossal statue in Stormwind's Valley of Heroes honors his deed. In Aerie Peak, High Thane Falstad took command.

The human kingdoms later quarreled and fractured, but the Wildhammers remained loyal partners of King Terenas Menethil II. During the Third War, the Scourge swept across Lordaeron. Wildhammer flyers took to the skies again, fighting to defend allied lands and innocent refugees from the walking dead.

faq.q: Where is the Wildhammer clan based right now?
faq.answer: The Wildhammer clan is based at Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands, north of the Wetlands and the Thandol Span.

faq.q: Why don't the Wildhammers live in Ironforge?
aliases: war of the three hammers wildhammer
faq.answer: The Wildhammers lost the civil war for Ironforge to the Bronzebeards after High King Modimus Anvilmar died. Thane Khardros led the clan north to Grim Batol rather than live under Bronzebeard rule.

faq.q: What happened to their fortress at Grim Batol?
faq.answer: The Dark Iron sorceress Modgud besieged Grim Batol during the War of the Three Hammers. Thane Khardros slew her, but her sorcery corrupted the halls and made the mountain uninhabitable, driving the clan to the Hinterlands.

faq.q: Who leads the Wildhammer clan today?
faq.answer: High Thane Falstad Wildhammer leads the clan from Aerie Peak. He took command after Kurdran Wildhammer joined the Alliance Expedition through the Dark Portal.

faq.q: How did the Wildhammers join the Alliance?
faq.answer: During the Second War, Orgrim Doomhammer attacked the Hinterlands as he marched toward Quel'Thalas. Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar led the Alliance in defense of Aerie Peak, driving off the Horde and forest trolls. The Wildhammers joined the Alliance of Lordaeron in gratitude for their aid.

faq.q: Are the Wildhammer dwarves closely allied with Ironforge?
aliases: do ironforge and wildhammer get along
faq.answer: Yes. Though the clans fought during the War of the Three Hammers, they united against the Dark Irons. They built the Valley of Kings in Loch Modan to honor their friendship and have kept a firm alliance ever since.

angles.text: As a dwarf of Ironforge, you share kinship with the Wildhammers through old oaths. They favor windy crags and open skies over deep mines, and their stormhammer bravery commands deep respect.
The Alliance owes much of its strength in the skies to Wildhammer gryphon riders. Their lightning-infused mounts helped turn the tide against the Horde's red dragons during the Second War.
The bond Wildhammer mountaineers share with wild gryphons shows beast mastery built on lifelong partnership rather than simple dominion.
Wildhammer tradition channels raw storm energy through mystic hammers and keeps a bond with elemental lightning and nature, older than Ironforge's modern church traditions.
